problem_statement: LangChain's tool-calling pipeline has multiple structural weak points that surface across different providers and usage patterns. Developers who need to inject precomputed or programmatic tool results (for example, replaying a prior tool call/response pair) have no first-class API to do so; they must hand-craft AIMessage/ToolMessage pairs, which breaks under providers with strict validation such as Gemini's thought-signature checks, forcing lossy workarounds. Separately, the default tool-call parsers use broad exception handling, so a single malformed function dict in a batch silently drops every valid tool call alongside it, with no partial-success path and no visibility into what was lost. Streaming compounds this: some providers (e.g., OpenRouter) fragment tool-call arguments across SSE chunks, and LangChain's assembly logic can execute a tool prematurely with empty arguments, triggering validation errors and retry loops that run until the recursion limit is hit. Model-specific constraints are also not respected — forcing tool_choice='required' against reasoning/thinking models (e.g., qwen3.5-plus, deepseek-r1) causes hard 400 errors with no documented override. On the human-in-the-loop side, rejected tool calls can remain present in AIMessage.tool_calls, raising concern that a ToolNode invoked directly could still execute them, undermining confidence in reject semantics. Observability is incomplete: on_tool_start streaming events omit tool_call_id, making it impossible for UI consumers to attribute events to the correct call when parallel calls share a tool name. Tool call budgeting is reactive rather than proactive: ToolCallLimitMiddleware cuts the agent off after the fact instead of informing the model of its remaining budget, wasting calls and degrading planning. Finally, tool error-handling DX is inconsistent: a ToolException raised inside a @wrap_tool_call middleware handler is not caught at the agent level, forcing crashes, and handle_tool_error behavior differs undocumented between the @tool decorator and ToolNode.
target_user: Developers building LangChain-based agents that call tools programmatically or interactively — including those integrating multiple LLM providers (Gemini, OpenRouter, reasoning models), building human-in-the-loop approval flows, and building UI layers that stream tool-call progress to end users.

user_stories.persona: a developer integrating precomputed tool results
user_stories.action: inject prior tool call/response context through a first-class API instead of hand-crafting message history
user_stories.value: my integration doesn't break under strict provider validation like Gemini's thought signatures

user_stories.persona: a developer running batched tool calls
user_stories.action: have malformed function dicts isolated and reported instead of silently discarding the whole batch
user_stories.value: valid tool calls in the same batch still execute and I can see what failed and why

user_stories.persona: a developer using a streaming provider like OpenRouter
user_stories.action: have fragmented SSE tool-call argument chunks reassembled correctly before execution
user_stories.value: tools aren't invoked prematurely with empty arguments and my agent doesn't loop until the recursion limit

user_stories.persona: a developer using a thinking/reasoning model
user_stories.action: override or safely disable tool_choice='required' when the underlying model doesn't support it
user_stories.value: my agent doesn't fail with a 400 error just because I chose a reasoning model

user_stories.action: trust that a rejected tool call cannot be executed even if ToolNode is invoked directly
user_stories.value: reject semantics are enforced consistently regardless of code path

user_stories.persona: a developer building a UI that streams tool execution
user_stories.action: receive tool_call_id on on_tool_start event data
user_stories.value: I can correctly attribute streamed events to the right call even when parallel calls share a tool name

user_stories.persona: a developer configuring tool call limits
user_stories.action: have the LLM informed of its remaining tool-call budget during execution
user_stories.value: the agent plans within budget instead of being abruptly cut off mid-task

user_stories.persona: a developer handling tool errors in middleware
user_stories.action: have a ToolException raised inside @wrap_tool_call caught at the agent level with documented handle_tool_error behavior consistent across @tool and ToolNode

acceptance_criteria.given: a developer has a precomputed tool call and result
acceptance_criteria.when: they use the new injection API to add it to conversation state
acceptance_criteria.then: the message pair is accepted and replayed correctly by providers with strict validation such as Gemini, without manual AIMessage/ToolMessage construction

acceptance_criteria.given: a batch of tool calls contains one malformed function dict
acceptance_criteria.when: the default tool parser processes the batch
acceptance_criteria.then: all well-formed tool calls in the batch are still returned successfully and the malformed entry is reported as an isolated parse error

acceptance_criteria.given: a streaming provider splits tool-call arguments across multiple SSE chunks
acceptance_criteria.when: the stream is consumed by the agent
acceptance_criteria.then: the tool is invoked only once full arguments are assembled, and it is never invoked with empty {} arguments due to premature parsing

acceptance_criteria.given: an agent is configured with tool_choice='required' and a thinking/reasoning model backend
acceptance_criteria.when: the agent executes a tool-calling step
acceptance_criteria.then: the request either succeeds with an automatically adjusted tool_choice or the developer is given a documented, explicit override to avoid the 400 error

acceptance_criteria.given: a human reviewer rejects a proposed tool call
acceptance_criteria.when: ToolNode is invoked directly on the resulting AIMessage
acceptance_criteria.then: the rejected tool call is not executed

acceptance_criteria.given: two parallel tool calls of the same tool name are streamed
acceptance_criteria.when: on_tool_start events are emitted for each
acceptance_criteria.then: each event includes a tool_call_id that uniquely identifies its corresponding call

acceptance_criteria.given: an agent is running under ToolCallLimitMiddleware with a defined call budget
acceptance_criteria.when: the model is deciding whether to make another tool call
acceptance_criteria.then: the model is given its remaining call budget as part of context before the limit is reached

acceptance_criteria.given: a tool call raises a ToolException inside a @wrap_tool_call middleware handler
acceptance_criteria.when: the exception propagates up during agent execution
acceptance_criteria.then: the agent catches it according to documented handle_tool_error behavior instead of crashing, with identical behavior documented for both the @tool decorator and ToolNode paths

out_of_scope: Building a new UI layer for visualizing tool call streams (only event metadata is in scope)
Adding new providers beyond hardening support for existing ones (Gemini, OpenRouter, reasoning models already in use)
Redesigning the overall agent execution loop or ToolNode architecture beyond the specific fixes described
Automatic retry/backoff strategy redesign for tool call failures unrelated to parsing or streaming fragmentation

risks.description: Each pain point in this finding has a frequency of only one reported issue, so the evidence base is thin; prioritization across these eight fixes is based on severity labels rather than corroborated frequency, and real-world impact may differ from what a single report suggests.

The human-in-the-loop rejection concern (pain point 5) was explicitly noted as not reproducible via the standard create_agent path, meaning the underlying bug may be narrower or already mitigated, and engineering effort could be misallocated if this is not first confirmed as a genuine defect.

Hardening parsing and streaming logic to tolerate malformed or fragmented provider payloads risks masking genuine upstream provider bugs or introducing subtle behavior changes for providers that currently work correctly, requiring careful regression coverage across all supported providers.
Introducing a first-class API for injecting precomputed tool call context is a design-heavy change with potential backward-compatibility implications for existing message-replay-based integrations.
